text:
saranya: Seeing a weird hit-rate collapse on the prefix cache for the afternoon load. 85% -> 42% in ~10k requests, latency spiked ~30ms p50. Posting nsys timeline extract shortly. :confused:

jake: Which model + quantization? any kernel fallbacks in the trace?

saranya: gpt-medium-like from the catalog, int8 quantized variant. No explicit fallback error, but kernel timings look different mid-run. Attached a tiny trace snippet:
```
nsys timeline: kernel_launch 0-120s
  conv_gemm_fast  : 0-300us (steady)
  gemm_fallback   : 320-750us (+ spikes)
  kv_lookup       : 40-70us (drops to 8us later)
  kv_write        : 12-20us
```
Notice gemm_fallback starts showing intermittently at 11:34:10.

perf-bot: automated-note: collected nsys: /artifacts/nsys/run-1768023456.qdrep, perfetto: /artifacts/perfetto/1768023456.pb

olivia: Quick check — are we hitting a kernel selection threshold: seqlen distribution changed? A few clients sent lots of short prompts?

saranya: seq len stayed about the same median 34, but tail increased (95p 120 -> 300). Could that flip kernel choice?

mike: Yes, our kernel selector uses sequence-length buckets + occupancy estimate. If tail increases, it may prefer a fallback kernel that favors longer sequences but is slower for short ones. Also batching heuristics could change batch composition and cause different kernel to be chosen.

jake: Can you paste the kernel-selection table snapshot from the trace? Even the small CSV output helps.

saranya: pasted: `kernel_selector.csv` lines: 
"bucket","kernel","score"
"<64","conv_gemm_fast",0.92
"64-256","gemm_mixed",0.87
">256","gemm_fallback",0.78
We started seeing >256 entries jump at 11:34:08.

olivia: That aligns. When batcher sees a few long in-flight sequences, it switches to the conservative kernel for the whole micro-batch to avoid OOMs. But we should be able to still prefer fast kernel for short sequences via sub-batching policy. Are we applying sub-batching?

mike: Not currently for dedicated inference path; we only enable sub-batching under stress. If the dispatcher misestimates GPU occupancy, it may disable sub-batching. Check the batcher log: `batch_policy: adaptive, subbatch: disabled, occupancy: 0.74`

saranya: batcher log around event: `2026-01-29T11:34:09Z DEBUG dispatcher: switched_kernel=gemm_fallback reason=tail_seqlen`

jake: Also look at KV cache hit pattern. You said kv_lookup drops to 8us later — is that because we evicted warm prefixes? Share a kv-stats dump.

saranya: kv-stats: total_accesses=18432, hits=7712 (41.8%), warm_prefixes=128 -> 32 after the spike. Eviction rate rose at same timestamp.

olivia: Eviction could be due to increased memory pressure from the fallback kernel (higher temporary allocations). Kernel fallback often needs extra workspace. If that bumped memory usage we might evict cache entries. 

mike: Good call. If cache entries get evicted, subsequent requests become cold and longer sequences will further push kernel choice to conservative side -> feedback loop. Looks like a positive feedback loop.

jake: Suggestion: run a targeted nsys with NVTX marks around the kernel-selector branch and KV LRU ops to confirm ordering. Use low-latency captures (sampling 10s windows) to avoid huge files. Example: `nsys profile --sample=cpu --trace=cupti,cuda,nvtx -o ./tmp/trace --capture-range nvtx` then replay a short synthetic workload with a mix of short/long prompts.

olivia: I'll reproduce with synthetic mix and enable sub-batching override to force fast kernel for short items. Also will disable adaptive eviction temporarily to see if cache stays stable.

saranya: Thanks. If we confirm, mitigation options: 1) Make kernel selector more robust to transient tail by using decayed metrics instead of instant bucket counts. 2) Prefer sub-batching when mixed-length batches detected. 3) Tighten eviction thresholds when kernel workspace expands.

perf-bot: action-items created: PERF-678: reproduce trace + nvtx marks, PERF-679: conservative-kernel hysteresis, PERF-680: eviction-threshold adjust.

mike: One more data point — add a quick histogram of per-token extra workspace per kernel. We can quantify memory delta and set a safe margin.

saranya: On it. Will run the reproduce now and post artifacts link. Thanks all :thumbsup:

olivia: I'll follow up with a small PR to enable sub-batching override flag.

jake: great, keep the nsys qdrep and the perfetto timeline, they help correlate exact order.

saranya: Uploaded artifacts: /artifacts/nsys/1768023456-repro.qdrep, /artifacts/perfetto/1768023456-repro.pb. End of thread.
